message: Weight coming back after stopping treatment is biology, not failure — so plan for maintenance from day one.
reasoning: Regain is the #1 fear in our GLP-1 user research ('agar band kiya toh sab wapas?'). This trial answers it honestly: yes, most of it came back when BOTH the medicine and lifestyle support stopped — but not all, and the body's pushback is biological, not a willpower failure. That replaces shame with a plan and points to a doctor-led maintenance conversation, without promoting any drug (CDSCO March 2026).

scenes.vo: What happens a year after people stop a weight-loss injection? A big trial followed them.
Over 68 weeks of treatment, people lost 17.3% of their weight on average.
Then the injection and the lifestyle support both stopped. Within a year, about two-thirds came back.
Still, they stayed 5.6% below where they started, and 48.2% kept off at least 5%.
Why? After weight loss, the body triggers changes that push weight back up. Regain is common.
Here, lifestyle support stopped too, which the authors say may have added to the regain.
Talk to a steer doctor about a long-term plan that fits you.
Weight-loss injection band karne ke ek saal baad kya hota hai? Ek bade trial ne yahi dekha.
Treatment ke 68 hafton mein, log average 17.3% weight kam kar paaye.
Phir injection aur lifestyle support, dono band. Ek saal mein lagbhag do-tihaai weight wapas aa gaya.
Phir bhi, shuruaat se 5.6% kam rahe, aur 48.2% log 5% se zyada kam pe tike rahe.
Kyun? Weight kam hone par body khud aise changes karti hai jo weight wapas badhaate hain.
Is trial mein lifestyle support bhi band hua tha, aur authors kehte hain isse regain badh sakta hai.
steer ke doctor se baat karo, apne liye sahi long-term plan samjho.

caption_en:
"If I stop, will it all come back?" It's the question we hear most. In the STEP 1 extension, 327 adults stopped a weekly weight-loss injection AND their lifestyle support at week 68. A year later, about two-thirds of the lost weight had returned — but on average they were still 5.6% below where they started, and 48.2% kept off at least 5%.

Regain isn't a willpower failure; after weight loss the body pushes back. So any plan needs an exit plan. Note: most participants were White adults in 5 high-income countries, and several authors work for the manufacturer.

Source: Wilding et al., Diabetes Obes Metab 2022 (doi:10.1111/dom.14725)
